sentences.text: Fossils of Luperosuchus come from the Chañares Formation in Argentina, where only a single atlas intercentrum and an incomplete skull have been preserved. The preserved part of the skull measures 54.5 cm, suggesting a total length of about 60 cm. A tall, mediolaterally compressed crest sits on the front of its snout.
Romer noted fused sutures in the skull, indicating the specimen was mature, and later studies confirmed the bones were fully fused with well-developed sculpting.
The holotype specimen PULR 04 was collected by Ruth Romer on January 17, 1965, and Alfred S. Romer published the description of the genus Luperosuchus in 1971.
Luperosuchus was one of the largest carnivores in the Chañares Formation and one of the few large animals there.
The locality where the fossils were found provides a minimum age of 236.1 +/- 0.6 million years.
Romer originally classified Luperosuchus as a member of the family Rauisuchidae, and it is classified as a reptile.
Luperosuchus lived during the latest Ladinian stage of the late Middle Triassic or the earliest Carnian of the Late Triassic, specifically between 241.464 and 237 million years ago.

During the Ladinian period, between 241.464 and 237 million years ago, the early environment of Luperosuchus was a braided river system with periodic flooding, which later changed to include volcanic deposits like tuff and ash.
It is debated whether specimen PULR-V 057 belongs to Luperosuchus or represents a distinct taxon, with some researchers suggesting the differences are taxonomic rather than due to age.
